title: Shader Alchemy Pool
description: A magical pool scene where coffee mugs float on the water surface, each carrying a custom shader effect. The user mixes shader properties across mugs by dragging energy between them, with a conservation law ensuring total shader energy remains constant. Undo/redo support lets the user experiment freely.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load pool.glb as the central scene element scaled to fill the view, coffeeMug.glb instanced 4 times arranged in a diamond pattern floating on the pool surface, and ShadowmappableMesh.glb as a platform beneath the pool casting/receiving shadows. Set up a PerspectiveCamera at position (0,8,12) looking at the pool center. Add a DirectionalLight with shadow mapping enabled (2048x2048 shadow map) and an AmbientLight. Apply a custom ShaderMaterial to the pool surface simulating animated caustic water using vertex displacement (sine waves in the vertex shader) and a procedural caustic pattern in the fragment shader with a u_time uniform. Each coffee mug gets a unique ShaderMaterial with three tunable properties displayed as colored auras: glow intensity (red channel, 0-1), refraction strength (green channel, 0-1), and iridescence (blue channel, 0-1). The total energy across all four mugs for each channel must always sum to exactly 2.0 (conservation law). Implement click-drag interaction: click one mug to select it as source (highlight ring appears), then click another as target. A slider overlay appears allowing transfer of energy in 0.1 increments for each of the three channels simultaneously (multi-input coupling). The target mug gains what the source loses. Display each mug's current RGB energy values as floating labels using CSS2DRenderer. The ShadowmappableMesh platform shader should react to the average energy state of all mugs, shifting its surface pattern accordingly. Implement an undo/redo stack (minimum 20 states) toggled by on-screen buttons or Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Shift+Z. Show a HUD with total energy per channel to verify conservation. Add a reset button restoring equal distribution (0.5 each). The water caustic animation should continuously run. All interactions require 10-14 steps to fully redistribute energy into a target configuration shown as a goal state in the corner of the screen.
